name: Pettnau
kurzbeschreibung: Municipality in the district of Innsbruck-Land in the Inn Valley west of Innsbruck, characterised by agriculture, commuters and a rural residential character.
beschreibung:
Overview

Pettnau is situated in the central Inn Valley in the district of Innsbruck-Land at an altitude of 628 metres on the northern banks of the Inn River, approximately 20 kilometres west of the regional capital Innsbruck between Zirl and Telfs. This idyllic residential municipality is home to around 1,115 residents and spans an area of 10.8 square kilometres, about two-thirds of which is densely forested. The municipality encompasses several traditional hamlets, including Leiblfing, Tiefental, Unterpettnau, Mitterpettnau, Oberpettnau, Kellertal, and Dirschenbach. Pettnau enjoys a sunny hillside location beneath the colossal southern precipices of Mount Hohe Munde (2,662 m) and the Mieming Chain. The village is best known as a tranquil haven away from mass tourism, celebrated for its river rafting and coaching heritage along the ancient transit corridor, the iconic hilltop Church of St. George in Leiblfing, and the rich Gaisau nature reserve across the river.

History

The name Pettnau derives from the Middle High German word Pette, referring to a historic ferry and timber rafting post on the river; fittingly, the municipal coat of arms depicts Saint Christopher, the patron saint of ferrymen and travellers. Historical roots run deep: the largest hamlet, Leiblfing, was first documented in 1238 in the archives of Wilten Abbey, tracing back to a Bavarian noble settlement of the Libolvinger clan, while an earlier Romanesque church is recorded as early as 1090. A paramount cultural monument is the Parish Church of St. George in Leiblfing, perched on an isolated hillock: its bell tower features a singular architectural blend of a Baroque onion dome crowned by a Gothic spire – according to legend, the result of a local compromise in 1710 when villagers could not agree on a single style. Another historic treasure is the Mellaunerhof estate, recorded in 1291 as one of Tyrol's oldest inns, serving for centuries as a vital coaching post and salt trading station.

Getting There

Pettnau boasts exceptional transport connections while preserving its rural peace. Motorists travel directly via the Inntal Autobahn A12, using the Telfs-Ost exit from the west or Zirl-West from the east, or via the toll-free federal road B171, taking just 20 minutes from Innsbruck city centre. Rail passengers utilize the nearby stations of Telfs-Pfaffenhofen or Hatting on the Arlberg Railway, served every 30 minutes by Tyrolean S-Bahn lines S4 and S5. Hatting station lies on the opposite bank of the Inn and connects to Pettnau via a pedestrian and bicycle bridge in just a few minutes. Additionally, frequent VVT regional bus routes 4130 and 4176 provide direct public transit linking all hamlets directly with Telfs, Zirl, and Innsbruck.

Tips

The hilltop Church of St. George in Leiblfing is one of the most photographed heritage landmarks in the Inn Valley, with its picturesque silhouette set against the towering limestone wall of Hohe Munde. Directly across the river, the 27-hectare Gaisau Nature Reserve beckons nature lovers: this rare wetland sanctuary of riparian woodland, reed beds, and Siberian iris blooms provides an essential breeding haven for kingfishers, woodpeckers, and amphibians. Cyclists can pedal along the family-friendly Inn Valley Cycle Path R1, while long-distance hikers follow the Tyrolean Way of Saint James along the riverbank. For alpine enthusiasts, panoramic forest trails ascend towards the Mieming Plateau, peaceful Lake Mösern, and the famous Peace Bell of the Alps.
